utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecutor's Exhibit 652.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am referring, Mr. Usher, to paragraph 4 of this document. It should be at the top of "Novi Travnik."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let me read this. It's in English, unfortunately, and not in your native tongue, so I will attempt to read it as slowly as possible. It deals with Novi Travnik, and it notes as follows: "A liaison officer team reported that tensions are still high in Novi Travnik. A local source (Croatian) stated that he believed the Croats in Novi Travnik were going to try and instigate trouble amongst the Croats and Muslims. Comment. If the talks in Geneva are unsuccessful, they may use this as a reason to initiate troubles among Croats and Muslims. Comment ends." My question for you, General, is is it true that if the Croats believed that they were unsuccessful in Geneva, that they were going to use that as an excuse to cause problems with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Please, could you just tell me the date that this document or, rather, this comment refers to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, General. The date is 8 January, 1993. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that there was tension at the time in Novi Travnik, and they were running high. Primarily, there were tensions between the members of different military groups, and we made a maximum effort, with the assistance of the U.N., in order to take care of all the problems and to ease the tensions. Part of my command was in Novi Travnik so that they would resolve all these incidents and conflicts. I don't know. I'm not aware of any planned provocation of trouble, because we were still working together against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in your discussions with Bruno Stojic, did he discuss with you the fact that the HVO was going to enforce this plan militarily, whether or not the Serbs and the Muslims signed on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he did not discuss it with me. He talked to me in the following terms, that the plan would be implemented when everybody signed it, and my main question was demobilisation and joint command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet, General, you testified that on the 9th of January, the Bruno Busic Brigade came to Novi Travnik and the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade came to Vitez; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct. But these were not brigades; these were battalions. Because Bruno Busic had, perhaps, about 100 men and Ludvig Pavlovic about 50, so these were not brigades; they were battalions. The point of them coming were joint activities, first and foremost, in order to stabilise the front line at Travnik because at that time, there was also a joint command that was operating. Before all negotiations, talks, agreements, et cetera, the situation would usually be less stable throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who sent them there, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, either Bruno Stojic or he would authorise the head of the main staff to send them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that they were coming?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When they came, then I found out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told when you were in Mostar on the 6th of January that three days later, two units were going to come to Novi Travnik and come to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That request for their arrival was sent a lot earlier. Possibly this was discussed, but I do not recall that in particular. I would have to look it up. I know that there was a request put in by the joint command, but it was considerably earlier. Let me just have a look. No. In my chronology, there's no mention of any discussion with Bruno Stojic specifically with regard to that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall being informed prior to their arrival that they were coming, given the fact that you were the Central Bosnia Operative Zone commander?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I already said that I was aware of the fact that a request was put in. Perhaps I was informed too. But this request stemmed from the meeting between General Pasalic, Prkacin, Dzemo Merdan, and myself, that we would need forces, intervention forces, and for the stabilisation of the front line. Possibly I was aware of this, but I'm not too sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, just by way of clarification, would it be fair to say that all of your conversations with Bruno Stojic are not in the chronology that you testified to on direct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All main questions that I had and that I discussed with Bruno Stojic, I highlighted here as regards the 6th of January, 1993. That's the meeting I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, by the time the Bruno Busic Brigade and the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade got to Novi Travnik and Vitez respectively, Prkacin was no longer involved in activities in Central Bosnia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not aware of when his activity stopped. I know that from time to time he would come to Zenica as a member of the joint command. He would stay in Vitez, Travnik, sometimes in Mostar. I really do not have the precise date when this activity of his stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, clearly by the beginning of January of 1993, Prkacin was not part of any joint command any more; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I already said that I do not know about that, because when he was appointed a member of the joint command, this was done by a public decision of the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at a press conference in Busovaca. But I do not know when a public decision was passed that this post of his had expired. He was my superior, and I was in no position to ask him when his term would expire and whether he had the right documents or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, when did he stop being your superior?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that moment when orders were issued to him, when his post as member of the joint command was no longer operative --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General, please try to make an effort. We are talking here of military issues and not about civilian matters, so you must know when one of your superiors ceased being one of your superiors.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, he was my superior, but others appointed him irrespective of me. So I don't know honestly. He probably received orders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General, you are a General, so you must worry about who is your superior. Would you please look through your documents, your personal chronology, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know who my superior is, Your Honours, but the precise date when General Prkacin's and General Pasalic's terms expired, that, I do not know. They were members of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. This will be taken down. Mr. Kehoe, you may move forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this particular unit, the first one, the Bruno Busic Brigade, were they HV soldiers, I mean, soldiers of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not of the brigade. There's a great difference between a brigade and a battalion. There's a major difference. They were not brigades; they were battalions. One was at company level. These are HVO units that were established and organised by the Department of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to these battalions, were these HV soldiers, soldiers of the Republic of Croatia, in the Bruno Busic Battalion?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, because these are units that are not from the structure of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, but as far as I know, they were members of the HVO, I'm saying, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They came from Mostar. In one, there were almost 100 soldiers, and in the other one, there were almost 50 soldiers, that is to say, that the total number of these soldiers is approximately 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, these particular soldiers, as soon as they came to Central Bosnia and Novi Travnik and to Vitez, began to commit many crimes, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Novi Travnik, those who arrived in Novi Travnik, they did commit disciplinary offences because they immediately appropriated part of the hotel for themselves, and they moved into this hotel. The same was done by this unit. They took part of a school, and they stayed at this school, and they did not wait for the regular procedure or for someone to ensure this for them. These were soldiers for these intervention actions, and there were quite a few problems, at any rate, in terms of their behaviour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the particular crimes that they committed first in Novi Travnik? I mean, were they accused of being involved in rapes? Were they accused of being involved in shootings and beatings of the local population? Tell us a little about that.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know of an incident. Fire was opened in the office of one of the commanders on the side of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and later on, they acted against the Territorial Defence. There were also arrests, mutual arrests, that is to say, these soldiers arrested Territorial Defence soldiers, and the other way around, Territorial Defence soldiers arrested members of that unit. Also, one rape was reported, and I believe that there were other such offences. Therefore, I asked the assistant for security of the Operative Zone to be transferred with his office and with his men to Novi Travnik and that in Novi Travnik he make an effort to stabilise the situation and investigate all of this, and that is what he did, in keeping with what I had asked for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, to be specific, this was a rape by a member of the Bruno Busic Battalion against a Muslim woman in Novi Travnik; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This was one case of rape, and I already said that this case was processed and prosecuted, and the assistant for security made his own investigation and report in this respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your testimony that this particular soldier in the Bruno Busic Battalion was disciplined and prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am asserting that this case of rape was investigated, and it was completed by providing information and also the findings of the investigation to Mostar, to the security office there. This was not in the structure of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, and I don't know how and in which way this case was taken further, that is to say, what the district military court in Mostar did in respect to this soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let us take what you just said. You said that the investigation was transferred down to Mostar. Who in Mostar was responsible for ensuring that this case was prosecuted or that this soldier was disciplined? Who? Give us a name.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, at any rate, an officer of the security administration who acquainted the public prosecutor in Mostar with this crime, and he also filed a criminal report. The district prosecutor in Mostar was supposed to take further action in terms of prosecution with regard to this crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, who is the person who is responsible for continuing this criminal prosecution in Mostar? Do you know anybody?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not in charge of the district military courts, and they had their own establishment in the Ministry of Defence and within this administration. I do not know the names of the officials there in the courts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move to discipline. Was this soldier disciplined for the rape of this Muslim woman?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In principle, it was as follows: If it was a crime, then the crime would be prosecuted by district military courts, and if it is a question of a disciplinary infraction, then this would be taken care of by commanders at the appropriate level, that is to say, that if someone is prosecuted for a crime, then that is not at the same time a disciplinary infraction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you told us previously that you were interested in peaceful negotiations with the Muslims. Do you think it was important for the Muslims to know whether or not this particular soldier had been disciplined or prosecuted for this rape? Do you think that was significant for relations between the Muslims and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It certainly was important, and I personally called the commander from Novi Travnik, Mr. Malbasic, and I asked him that a meeting be held with the representatives of the Muslim Bosniak people, that is to say, the representatives of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that at that meeting, they be acquainted with all the difficulties related to problems of structure in terms of command, supervision, command and control, the chain of command over such units. This meeting was held between both commanders, and Colonel Stewart gave us a lot of assistance in this attempt to stabilise the situation and to avoid a conflict, after all the incidents in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure you gathered the information on what happened to this rapist and passed it on to the Bosnian authorities in Novi Travnik to assist in easing tensions. Did you do that and what did you tell them the punishment was that this soldier received?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that the meeting was held at the level of commanders of brigades, and I believe that the commander of the brigade, Borislav Malbasic, shared all his information. I asked him to make it known that these cases would be taken care of, that is to say, that they would be investigated, that it would be established who did it, and that measures would be taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you don't know of any punishment that was given to this rapist, do you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that these records were kept by the district military court. During my testimony, I already said that from January until March 1993, there were 92 crimes that were committed by persons in uniform and that 31 criminal reports were filed and that three rulings were passed by the district military court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is this, General: You do not know of any punishment that was given to this rapist for the crime he inflicted on this Bosnian Muslim woman, do you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe the court took care of this. I don't know what the punishment was and for how long, but I am deeply convinced that the court did do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to this crime, there were numerous crimes committed by the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade that was located in Vitez; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were incidents that they committed to, but there were incidents on both sides. On one side were HVO units that were brought from elsewhere, and then there were special purpose units from that part that were joined in. On the other side were the same kind of units from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking now about the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade, and I'd ask you, General, to reserve your comments just for the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade. My question concerning the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade is that after they came to Vitez on the 8th of January, they committed numerous crimes in the Vitez area; didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that they disturbed public law and order together with other groups in the territory of Vitez, and I already wanted to mention that there were different groups that caused problems and difficulties and disturbed the public law and order. There were also crimes, certainly. This figure that I gave you shows that, 92 for the first three months of the year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us talk about, first, the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade. How many members of the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade were either disciplined or prosecuted for crimes they committed in the Vitez area in January of 1993? How many?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot give an exact answer as to how many, because that brigade or, rather, that unit had its own chain of command, and it is well-known that the commander of that unit was in charge if disciplinary infractions were committed, but if crimes were committed, then reports were filed to those who were in charge of prosecuting crimes, and those were district military courts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is your answer, General, that you do not have any information about members of the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade either being disciplined or prosecuted for crimes that they committed in Vitez or the Vitez area in January of 1993? Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I personally do not have information here with me, because these units were not directly subordinated to me. These are not units belonging to the structure of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. These were units of the Ministry of Defence. They can be subordinated to the main staff at a given point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, 1.00. I was about to move to another document. I don't know if Your Honour wants to break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Absolutely. The hearing is adjourned and we will resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please be seated. Mr. Kehoe, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, we were talking, prior to the break at lunch, that the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade was in Vitez and -- excuse me, Ludvig Pavlovic Battalion, as well as the Bruno Busic Battalion being in Novi Travnik while the Ludvig Pavlovic Battalion was in Vitez. Now, we ended up talking about the Ludvig Pavlovic Battalion, and they were garrisoned with the Vitezovi in the Dubravica school, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that they were billeted in Dubravica. I don't know whether they were together with the Vitezovi, because the Vitezovi also used a motel which is called Ribnjak in Kruscica, Ribnjak or "fishpond." So I don't know at that time whether they were together or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in January of 1993, were some Vitezovi soldiers billeted at the Dubravica school?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know if they were. It is possible, because they had their own command and control system, and they were completely independent of my own command. I'm not sure whether the Vitezovi were in the school. Perhaps part of them were, but I'm really not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, the conflict between the HVO and the BiH, or the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, broke out in Gornji Vakuf on the 11th of January, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The conflict in Gornji Vakuf between the BH army and the HVO broke out in the first half of January 1993. I am not sure of the exact date but it is possible that that was the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's, for reference purposes, just clarify the date if we can, to the best of our ability, with a milinfosum, again another British battalion military information summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can, Mr. Registrar, I believe the usher is otherwise occupied. Oh, there he is. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 653.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just read you, for date purposes, General, a portion of the military information summary of the Cheshire Battalion of 11 January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I would like to go to page 3 of this document, at the paragraph that begins: "At 1705."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll read it slowly for you, General. I realise it is in English. Let me start by saying this is a military information summary, General, for 11 January 1993. "At 1705, Gornji Vakuf operations room reported that fighting among the Croats and Muslims had started with the sound of small-arms fire and mortars coming from town. The BiH commander stated that the attacks had been initiated by the HVO and that the BiH were holding their positions. Four civilian injuries were reported so far. "At 2550, Gornji Vakuf operations room reported that sporadic small-arms fire was occurring frequently. The Muslims are reported to have sealed the town and fortified their checkpoints. There were reported to be a group of approximately 30 HOS soldiers on the main road to Bugojno. Comment. These may be in position to obstruct any possible BiH reinforcements from Bugojno. Comment ends." Now, General, does that refresh your recollection on the approximate day that the conflict broke out in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This does refresh my memory, and as I said, the conflict in Gornji Vakuf took place in the first half of January, 1993, and the conflict broke out between the HVO and the BH army there, corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, just to bring us geographically in place, the town of Prozor that we talked about this morning is on a major communications route that moves up to Central Bosnia; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. If you take the road from Tomislavgrad then the town of Prozor is on that main highway. However, if you take the route from Jablanica and Konjic there is a different road. There is another alternate route through from Gola Brda to Konjic which bypasses the town of Prozor and it goes via Kresevo to Kiseljak. You could reach Central Bosnia without going through the town of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We've got to protect our client, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I can understand that. The conflict is spreading, it seems. Please be careful, Mr. Usher. All right. Is it in place?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could stand up there, because I believe the witness has to lean to the side of the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, if you could stand up at this map and take the pen, and if you could show us where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If the two Defence counsels want to get nearer, of course, they can do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, I'd like to take a look at this map and -- we're going to have to move this over a little bit. I'll use the microphone right here. Thank you very much. We talked this morning about the HVO taking control of the town of Prozor. Would you take that marker and circle the town of Prozor? That's fine. Sure.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we just noted that the conflict had broken out in the town of Gornji Vakuf on the 11th of January. Can you circle the town of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think that you wanted me to circle Gornji Vakuf, the Upper Vakuf rather than the Donji Vakuf, which is what I heard. (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we also mentioned that the Bruno Busic Battalion was in Novi Travnik. Could you circle the town of Novi Travnik on that map? Down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, we have the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade in the town of Vitez. Could you circle that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, between Prozor and Vitez a main communication route would take the route that connects these circles, wouldn't it? Prozor to Gornji Vakuf to Novi Travnik and then down to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. There's several roads. They were built during the war, from the time of the Serbian aggression, and these are mountain roads. But I know that there are roads from Prozor to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is the main route, is it not, from Prozor up through to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There are several roads going from Gornji Vakuf to Vitez. You could go either through Novi Travnik or through Sebesic or through Fojnica. The roads forked there, but it's all mountain -- it's a mountainous region and for the most part these were macadam roads through the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I would like you to mark the road that you would take from Prozor to Gornji Vakuf to Novi Travnik and to Vitez. Could you mark that route? I ask you to just press hard so that everybody can see it.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, if one were to travel from Prozor to Mostar, and I realise that Mostar is not on the map, leaving Prozor, which way would one travel?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are again two ways: One is a mountain road over Mount Vran to Tomislavgrad and then on to Mostar, and the second one is from Prozor down towards Jablanica and then again further down along the Neretva River Valley to Mostar. So there were, in essence, two roads, even though during the war there were some alternate routes which were built there, and I can find them if you want.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can mark those two routes that you were talking about, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. You can have a seat. General, at the time of the commencement of hostilities in Gornji Vakuf on the 11th of January, the HVO was in control of Prozor and had special units garrisoned in both Novi Travnik and in Vitez; is that an accurate picture of things as of the 11th of January?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you can just clarify it for me, when you're talking about Prozor, are you referring to the town of Prozor or to the municipality of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just the town, sir.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is possible that the HVO -- I assume that they had control over the town itself, and on 11 January, 1993, special purpose units were still in Travnik and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you were in communication with your colleagues in Gornji Vakuf during this period of time continuously assessing the situation, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was occasionally in contact with the commander of the northwestern Herzegovinian Operative Zone. I was concerned about the situation in Gornji Vakuf because the 3rd Corps of the BH army took part in this conflict, that is, the 3rd Corps from Zenica, in other words, the one which had their forces deployed in Vitez, Busovaca, Travnik, and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the fighting was going on in Gornji Vakuf, you were making preparations to launch activities in Central Bosnia, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The units under my command did not take part in the conflict in Gornji Vakuf, but the units of the 3rd Corps, which shared the area with me, did take part in this fighting in Gornji Vakuf. I was, of course, concerned about this because the entire movement of both the troops and the materiel was taking place in the area which was shared with the HVO. I had ordered the reconnaissance and monitoring of the movements of these troops, but there were no special measures or steps taken in order to provoke a conflict with the BH army. Obviously, the monitoring was stepped up because a lot of combat units of the 3rd Corps were being sent to -- just to be very specific, the combat units of the BH army were being sent over to Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, before we get into the actual details beginning on the 12th of January, let me reference you to a document, this is a part of the diary from Lieutenant Colonel Stewart, and the reference that we are going to discuss is the reference as of Tuesday, 12 January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 654.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this again is in English, and I will read it to you. It's at the bottom of the page, Mr. Usher. "Tuesday 12 January. Novi Travnik was surprisingly quiet overnight. I had ordered that the Standby Platoon was to go in there at 0900hrs and that Andrew MacDonald was to assume responsibility for the area - if necessary backing it all up with another platoon. For my part I wanted to see Blaskic; as we had been told by the HVO that he was the authority for anything that happened with regard to the HVO. It was much the same story with Vares a few weeks ago. Blaskic does seem to be the power in 'HVO Land.'" Now, General, in reference to that particular comment by Lieutenant Colonel Stewart, I would like to show you yet another milinfosum of 12 January, 1993, and I'd like to talk about these two items together.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 655.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The first item is going to be on page 2 of this milinfosum dated 12 January, 1993. It has "1992" on the top. I'm sorry; it does say "1993." I look to page 2, paragraph 3, "Novi Travnik," which starts, "The situation ..." and I'll read this again slowly, General. "The situation is still extremely tense with both sides appearing to be unable to talk to each other and the HVO using any excuse to antagonise the situation. Following the prisoner exchange on the 10th Jan., Major Malbasic claimed he had received a letter from Colonel Blaskic (the HVO district commander) questioning his decision to authorise the prisoner exchange and speak to UNPROFOR. Comment. Colonel Blaskic appears keen to antagonise the situation between Croats and Muslims in Novi Travnik. Comment ends." General, you told us that during this period of time, you were attempting to accommodate and resolve problems with the Muslims, yet you're complaining about a prisoner exchange that takes place on the 12th of January; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, and allow me to make a comment here. On 12 January, 1993, I had a meeting with Colonel Stewart on the situation in Novi Travnik, but this is a completely different situation as per the meeting which we held over the situation in Vares. After the meeting about Novi Travnik, I personally called Mr. Malbasic, who was the commander in Novi Travnik, and gave him specific tasks in order to calm down the situation, establishing contact with the commander of the 308th Brigade of Novi Travnik, that is, the BH army brigade. I also issued an order prohibiting breaking into private homes, this was an order specifically to Malbasic, and I gave him guidelines for the meeting with the 308th Brigade. It was to 1, calm down the situation; 2, investigate all incidents; and 3, return of the weapons and other equipment which had been taken. Also, in principle, I was advocating for all the exchanges to be done through the mediation of the ICRC and international organisations and the U.N. The U.N., as far as I knew, did not have the mandate for the prisoner exchanges. Only the Red Cross did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same day of the 12th of January, you also seized an ammunition truck of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina because you stated the truck was headed towards Gornji Vakuf; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not have such information. I know about the equipment, that it had been taken away, and the reason for it was because it was not accompanied by any documents. It was being transported with the humanitarian aid. It consisted of about 50 uniforms. If you have any document or other reference, I can comment on it. This would have been a duty of the police, but they were subordinate to me in their daily tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let's look at the next page of this military information summary, page 3, the second to last paragraph which notes: "The commanding officer," talking about Colonel Stewart. "The commanding officer spoke to Colonel Blaskic late this afternoon. Colonel Blaskic stated that he had the BiH ammunition truck. He claimed to have intercepted it because its destination was Gornji Vakuf. Did he not want the ammunition to get to Gornji Vakuf, as he was worried that it would escalate the problem there." Now, I just asked you whether or not you had intercepted an ammunition truck and you said no. Do you want to change that answer?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I said that I did not remember that part, but I do remember the military equipment part. It is possible that in the zone of responsibility -- and here I would like to really make it very clear that this is the zone of responsibility of Novi Travnik. This is at least one level below me. I gave Malbasic a directive to exchange the weapons and the equipment which had been taken away. Now, I do not know what the army had intercepted, what they had taken away from the HVO. That I do not know at the other end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, at this particular period of time you and the HVO in Gornji Vakuf were part of a plan to take over canton 8 and 10, weren't you, for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was no general plan that I am aware of, and I really do not know of any such plan. In addition, this is a geographically isolated area -- I mean, a different area. This is part of the Vrbas River water system. For us in Central Bosnia, it was only significant as part of the communications. It was part of the Northwestern Herzegovina Operative Zone. But I talked to General Merdan about the fact that any movements of the army which went -- that is, the 3rd Corps, that went from Zenica to Gornji Vakuf should be announced in advance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you another document, General. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, this document is speaking of the situation on 12th January. 1993 did you explain, Mr. Kehoe? Not 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, the top of the document does reflect 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, would you accept it's 1993 and not 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, '93.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, I want you to look at page 2, almost in the middle, and more particularly the last sentence of that paragraph which Mr. Kehoe put to you. There is a comment there. "Colonel Blaskic appears keen to antagonise the situation between Croats and Muslims." Well now, as briefly as you can answer, was that comment accurate or not accurate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That comment is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: My next question is: Have you any reason to offer why the writer of this document would have stated an inaccuracy of that kind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is possible that he didn't have enough knowledge about all the problems of functioning within the HVO establishment. Even more than that, perhaps he was, like myself, taken by surprise since the law and order in Travnik were so disturbed. Perhaps I should dwell on this a bit longer. In Novi Travnik we had conflicts between Croats and Croats too, that is to say, between the HVO and the HVO. This was at the beginning of November when there was open fighting between the HVO of Jajce and the HVO of Novi Travnik. We also had a conflict between the HVO and the TO. We had a conflict between the HVO of Novi Travnik and the HOS from Novi Travnik. In January, it is only with ultimate efforts made by the TO and the HVO and Colonel Stewart, who gave patrols for the town of Novi Travnik. It is only in this way that we managed to alleviate the situation in Travnik and prevent the outbreak of a new conflict perhaps. Everything that is abnormal anywhere else was normal there, that is to say, abductions of persons, numerous incidents, et cetera. Most of my co-workers spent most of their time in Novi Travnik, and I was with Malbasic and I was also with the leadership of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Colonel Stewart might have misunderstood the situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, as far as I understood it a few minutes ago, because I haven't got the document here in front of me and I don't understand the language, but Colonel Stewart says that the situation was similar to the situation in Vares. If that is so, then in Vares the problem was between HVO soldiers and UNPROFOR soldiers, and I did not consider that to be a problem either. Then there was another matter when I met with Colonel Stewart. That was the repair of the bridge in Vares. I told him I was surprised why he was asking me for permission for him to repair the bridge. We were happy to have anyone help us and no permit was required. He insisted. "Well, I want you to allow me to do it," he said. Since he asked me for that kind of permission, I gave him that kind of permission, although until the present day I do not know what he needed that permission for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please move on, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, if I can. Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a minute. Judge Rodrigues has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, on this document we find a reference made to a conflict taking place in Novi Travnik, a conflict between Croats and Muslims. Do you have the document 650 before you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't have it before me here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Well, the registrar will take the necessary measures for you to have it before you in a minute. I'll start with my question. We have here a conflict between Croats and Muslims. Are we talking about Croatian Croats -- Croats from Croatia or Croats from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, in this document 650, we see the date of the 20th of October, 1992. This is the conflict between the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, and the Territorial Defence, that is to say, Croats from Bosnia and Muslims, Bosniaks from Bosnia, from the municipality of Travnik -- Novi Travnik, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: All right. I'll go on with my question. The chief of staff of the army of Republika Srpska, could he make a distinction between HV and HVO forces or not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, those were still the beginnings of the establishment of the HVO, not all had insignia but some soldiers did wear insignia. However, he was not in a position to see this conflict because the front lines of the Serb army are far away from Novi Travnik after all, but he could see the area where the conflict was taking place, and I believe that he could have distinguished between the troops that he was in a position to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: If we look at document 650, we see that answering a question put to you by Mr. Kehoe, you said that the reference that was made in paragraph 2 of that document to the HV forces was, in fact, a reference made to HVO. I think you corrected that. Is that right or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, the HVO did not leave the front line at Jajce. It did not. It says here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. I think that you answered a question put to you by Mr. Kehoe by saying that here one was supposed to read HVO and not HV.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Fine. But if you look at document 650, you will notice, at the end of the first paragraph, that a reference is made to conflicts taking place between Muslims and Croat forces in Novi Travnik. At the end of paragraph 2, we see that a reference is made to HV forces. Now, in paragraph 3, reference is made to the HV forces once again. In paragraph 8, entitled "Conclusion," we can also see there a reference made to HV forces. So if we try to establish links between this document, document 650, and document 655, we are able to see that there is, in both documents, a reference made to Croat forces. I would add that in document 650, we find at least four references made to HV forces, not to HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I already said the problem is that we are making comments on the tactical situation and the document 650 is on an operational/strategic level. This 1st Corps of the army of Republika Srpska had its headquarters in Banja Luka and it defended the most vital areas of Banja Luka from the point of view of the interests of the Serbs. That was the greatest military potential of the Serbs and it was the largest of all the corps they had. For example, he gives the problem of Orasje by the Sava River. That is north of Bosnia. It has nothing to do with Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, I'm sorry I'm interrupting you again, but this is my question: In document 650, we see that there are four references made to HV forces. If there was three times a reference made to HVO and then one reference made to the HV, then we might be entitled to think that there is a mistake in this document. But in the four cases, we are talking about the HV forces. So is it really a mistake or shouldn't we, in fact, read "HV" and not "HVO" in this document? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know for sure - I know for sure - that the units of the Croatian army were not in Jajce. The units of the Croatian army were not in Jajce, but I do not see the HVO mentioned in the document, although I haven't read it carefully. It practically doesn't say "HVO" anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I think I've understood what you meant. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Rodrigues. It was something that was important and that should have been raised. All right. Mr. Kehoe, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we can go to the next document, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 656 and 656A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, in this particular document, on the 15th of January, you are requesting information from the brigades or the Operative Zone of Tomislavgrad, the Ante Starcevic Brigade in Gornji Vakuf and also the brigade in Bugojno, and you note: "Please send us information on the situation in your Brigade's area of responsibility, with an emphasis on the current situation in Gornji Vakuf." Now, it was important for you, as we move into the middle of January 1993, to know exactly what was taking place in Gornji Vakuf, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is just an indicator that we did not have sufficient information about all these events and that we were forced to intervene and ask for information to be submitted to us on the situation in the zone of responsibility with emphasis on the current situation in Gornji Vakuf. I already said that the 3rd Corps, which was in the same area as the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, was taking part in the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we've understood your answer perfectly, General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us turn to another series of documents that were executed on the 15th of January, the same day where you request this information.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 657, 657A for the French version, and 657B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this is a document executed by Jadranko Prlic, then the president of the HVO for the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and reads as follows, dated 15 January, 1993: "In line with the agreements which were reached and signed at the International Conference on the Former Yugoslavia and the peace agreement in Bosnia and Herzegovina (the Geneva agreements), the HVO /Croatian Defence Council/ of the HZ HB /Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna/ reached a decision at a special meeting in Mostar on 15 January 1993: 1. All units of the BH /Bosnia and Herzegovina/ Army currently in regions 3, 8 and 10 which were proclaimed Croatian in the Geneva agreements are subordinate to the Command of the Main Headquarters of the HVO Armed Forces. 2. All units of the HVO Armed Forces currently in regions 1, 5 and 9 which were proclaimed Muslim in the Geneva agreements are subordinate to the Command of the General Staff of the BH Army Command. 3. Units of the Kiseljak and Kresevo HVOs whose municipalities are in region 7, remain under the command of the Main Headquarters of the HVO Command until a final agreement has been reached on the status of region 7. 4. This decision is deemed temporary and shall remain in force until the Geneva agreement on the organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina is finally signed. 5. The decision shall be implemented within 5 (five) days, starting from today, 15 January 1993. 6. The decision shall be implemented by the Head of the Defence Department of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." General, let us move to the next document, and we will look at these three documents in sequence, and this is the order of Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 658, 658A for the French version and 658B for the English version. As far as Prosecution Exhibit 657 is concerned, 657A is the French version and 657B is the English version, contrary to what appeared in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, on the 15th of January, the Defence Minister or the head of the defence department is Bruno Stojic, and he implements this order on the same day as Jadranko Prlic's order of the 15th. In the first paragraph of this order, number 1 reads: "1. The Main Headquarters of the HVO Armed Forces must immediately contact all Operations Zones and Staffs of the BH /Bosnia and Herzegovina/ Army in regions 3, 8, 10 and 1, 5 and 9 in order to implement the HZ HB HVO Decision," and it gives the number and "15 January 1993." "2. All units of the HVO Armed Forces and BH Army who refuse to acknowledge the command referred to in points 1 and 2 of the above-mentioned Decision of the HZ HB HVO must leave the region which they do not belong to." If we could move down to number 5. "5. Officers of the BH Army must also join the HVO Armed Forces Command at the level of the Operations Zones and Brigades in numbers proportionate to the number of soldiers at the front. 6. I forbid the engagement of any officers of the BH Army who have so far been influencing the break-up of relations between the Croatian and Muslim peoples and brought about all clashes which have had tragic consequences. 7. The deadline for carrying out this order is 1900 hours on 20 January 1993." Before we discuss this, let us move to the next document which is the order of Milivoj Petkovic, also on the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 659, Prosecution Exhibit 659A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this is Milivoj Petkovic's order of the same day, and we will not read all of the provisions here. Again, it is the order subordinating the BiH army to the HVO in provinces 3, 8, and 10. As we read point number 1 of this order: "1. All units of the HVO and the BH Army Armed Forces in provinces 3, 8 and 10 (the Croatian provinces) shall be placed under command of the HVO Main Staff, i.e., under the command of the Central Bosnia, North-West and South-East Herzegovina Operative Zone." This is now down to number 4. "4. Members and units of the HVO and the BH Army Armed Forces that fail to submit to the commands as stipulated in Items 1 and 2 of this Order must leave the territory of provinces they do not belong to, otherwise they will be considered paramilitary, and disarmed." If we turn the page, the deadline for this order is 20 January, 1993. Now, General, we have a series of orders that emanate from the president of the HVO, Jadranko Prlic, down to the Minister of Defence, Bruno Stojic, and then down to the Chief of Staff, Milivoj Petkovic, all taking place on the 15th of January, 1993. These orders, ending with Milivoj Petkovic's order, is an order to the Bosnian army to subordinate themselves to the HVO, and if they are not subordinated, they will be disarmed and considered to be paramilitaries. Is that an accurate reading of these series of orders, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It is not correct to interpret this series of orders in such a way, because in all these orders, the subordination of all BH army units to the HVO is requested but also of the HVO to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, subordination works both ways. The HVO should be subordinated to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in certain provinces and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, according to these orders, was supposed to be resubordinated to the HVO. The other thing I wish to say, since you showed me a series of three orders and I could not say a word about any of them, these are not all the relevant orders. There is one order that is missing, and I believe that this is no accident. This is the order of the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, that the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina issued the same kind of order on the 15th of January, and that order was repeated on several occasions, on television, in the media, on radio. From that order onwards, the authorities acted in that way, issuing these authorities. The document that was signed by Jadranko Prlic, this document is a decision of the civilian authorities, that is to say, the civilian authorities issued an order. This was signed by Jadranko Prlic. I never talked to him about this document, and I had never seen the document before. Document 658 that you showed to me here and which was signed by the head of the Defence Department of Herceg-Bosna, later the Minister of Defence, Bruno Stojic, was sent to the main staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina for their information, that is to say, that this was no secret. It was sent to the main staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it was sent to the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina for his information, and it was also sent to the administration of the military police. Also, in this document, 658, the item that was omitted orders the members of the military police -- these orders are issued by the head of the military police to establish checkpoints in the provinces, that is to say, that all levels of command are being skipped, the Operative Zone, and direct order is issued to the military to establish checkpoints irrespective of any other commander. In point 8 of document 658, it is quite obvious that the same level of command of the head of the military police and of the head of the main staff of the HVO, that their level is the same. Another thing, this document, I received 659 and it caused great concern in the Operative Zone. It was the subject of a separate meeting that I convened with all my commanders because it was impossible to carry this out in my Operative Zone. In Central Bosnia, I border with the forces of the 1st Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 3rd Corps, the 2nd Corps, and partly the 4th Corps too. Even if I had the best established army in the world, I could not resubordinate four corps to myself. Also, this order required from me, if I were to implement it, that in the Lasva Valley the BH army be subordinated to the HVO, but in Zepce the HVO should be subordinated to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Kakanj and Vares are not mentioned at all. What would the HVO do there and so on? After I read this order, I gave instructions to my subordinates that we should wait to receive instructions as to how this should be carried out, that this should be given to us by Milivoj Petkovic and Mr. Sefer Halilovic, but the order of the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was received also by the general staff of the BH army. There was one Minister of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who was the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this time it was Mr. Bozo Rajic. Before him was Mr. Jerko Doko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's stay with Bozo Rajic. Bozo Rajic issued a subordination order, as you described, which was immediately countermanded by President Izetbegovic, wasn't it? Immediately?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was broadcast on television on several occasions, but if you say so, it is possible. I don't know about this. I did not communicate with President Izetbegovic regarding that order at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at Exhibit 657 and look at the preamble, General. This is the order of Jadranko Prlic. There is no reference in that preamble or anywhere in that document -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could keep those documents with the witness, all of them, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at that document, General. There is no reference to any order of Bozo Rajic in the preamble, is there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In terms of contents, this order is identical to the one of Bozo Rajic, and in this preamble the reference is made to this. I guess he had more information on this. I was not involved in these negotiations in Geneva and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there is no reference to Bozo Rajic's order in this preamble?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not in the preamble. The contents of this order and Bozo Rajic's one are practically identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, General Blaskic and Mr. Kehoe. I'm a bit confused. Do we have that document or don't we have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is not the documents, Mr. President. Bozo Rajic issued an subordination order that was immediately countermanded by President Izetbegovic. We have this particular document, with a vote by the Croatian Defence Council in this decision in Mostar on 15 January 1993. The Bozo Rajic particular document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Because it's an important issue, I must insist on this. I'm sorry. The witness is telling us that this order can be understood when we read another identical order which has been issued by the officials of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and then we can understand better what General Blaskic is saying, i.e., that mutatis mutandis the HVO forces are going under the control of the BH army according to the Geneva agreement, but I was under the impression that the Geneva agreement had not been signed. Here the question is different, General Blaskic, and that will be my only question, in fact: These different decisions, are they unilateral decisions emanating from the HVO or are they the manifestation of some kind of agreement by which all parties involved accept the Geneva agreement? Is it unilateral, in which case, of course, the situation appears in a different light. Does it mean that the HVO forces are going to come under the control of the BiH army in regions 1, 5, and 9? It would be useless. But if it's not a unilateral decision emanating from the HVO, then the situation is rather different and I understand your answer better. That's the reason why I'm insisting on this particular issue. I don't have the answer to my own question at this moment of the debate. Maybe towards the end of the trial we'll have an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not know. In fact, I'm just learning today that President Izetbegovic did countermand an order of his minister. I did not know of this. I knew of the decision of Bozo Rajic, Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which essentially is identical to this order. At that time I did have the document number 659 in my file. Bozo Rajic's order was rebroadcast for a number of times in that period of time on television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Kehoe, please go on. Thank you, General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, Bozo Rajic was a Croat, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Bozo Rajic was a Croat and Jerko Doko was a Croat, because the Croats, according to the agreement with the Muslims, did get the Ministry of Defence, whereas the Muslims got the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next document, General, which is Prosecutor's 456/6. Now, General, this is your order of the 16th of January, 1993, the next day after this order was received from Milivoj Petkovic on subordinating ABiH units to the HVO with the threat to be considered paramilitaries or disarm. You issue a full combat readiness order for all HVO formations in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, including the Bruno Busic formation, Ludvig Pavlovic formation, the Vitezovi formation, the Travnik police department, and the 4th Military Police Battalion. You write as follows: "Pursuant to the order of the Mostar HVO headquarters, number 01-66/93, dated 15 January, 1993, and due to the open and deceitful aggression of Muslim forces all over the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which has caused scores of HVO members to be killed and a number of them to be wounded, as well as Croatian homes to be burned and the Croatian people driven out, for the purpose of the self-defence of the people and the territory of Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna I hereby order: "1. The full combat readiness of formations. "2. All HVO formations are to be in a maximum state of readiness." If we move four down you note that: "4. Muslims and HVO formations who disobey our orders are to be disarmed and isolated." On the next page, number 5, you tell the 4th Military Police Battalion that it is to control the traffic and confiscate equipment and weapons from all Muslim transports and put them at the disposal of the HVO forces. So one day after this subordination order, you put all of your troops on full combat readiness, and you tell the 4th Military Police Battalion to confiscate weapons from Muslim transports. Now, it sounds like you're getting ready for combat activities, doesn't it, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I just get the order, please, the previous one? The one of the 15th, please. The order on the subordination. Your Honours, this is not my order on the full combat alert but, rather, this is issued by General Petkovic, the one on temporary attachment. Document 659 has a registration number 01-70/93. This is the 659. The document 456/6, I refer to the order which I had received from the chief of the main staff, with registration number 01-66/93 of 15 January. In other words, I refer to another document. I believe that the heading was just copied from that order. In this order, the combat readiness level is requested to be raised to the highest level, and I believe that all the other items were copied as they were in the order 01-66/93 of 15 January. As far as disarming of the ethnic Muslim soldiers within the HVO, I know that this did not happen because I knew at the time that there were Bosniak Muslims there. The chief of operations in Novi Travnik was a Bosniak Muslim. He was never disarmed. As far as the tasks to the military police are concerned, we just saw that the Minister of Defence is issuing orders to the military police at the checkpoints, and I know that -- again, I think that the order of 01-66 was copied. I know there were no big problems around that because most of the convoys were coming through Gornji Vakuf at the time, and there are other things here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the first thing, this was an extremely significant event, putting the entire area on a full combat readiness, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me just tell you, to put the entire area to full combat readiness alert just means to raise alertness when the Minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina issues documents such as this, which was published for the first time publicly. So the situation was tense and we could not allow ourselves to just be lying in bed. So this is a regular military measure. This is something that you do when, in the vicinity, there are combat operations going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew, when you issued this order, that there was going to be a negative reaction from the Muslims from this subordination order issued by Prlic, Stojic, and Petkovic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My apologies. All Bosniak Muslim soldiers received this order from their Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, unless it was somebody else. We all received it from the same source, and I believe that they received it also from the Minister of Defence of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which certainly did cause some confusion on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you passed this order down to your subordinate brigades, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I receive an order from the chief of main staff, at least I am obliged to send it down to my subordinate brigades, but there's also a remark in the order as to the method of distributing it. I sent it to them, and I told the brigade commanders at a meeting which was called only on that issue. On the 14th I had a regular meeting and on the 16th I had an extraordinary meeting with them precisely with respect to these issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the full combat readiness order is one step below a preparation combat order which then leads to the actual combat order; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. This is not part of any doctrine of any army. You can give full combat readiness on the first degree, second, third degree. You can do it when you have an exercise, when you have some major events going on in a neighbouring country. The preparatory combat order is what precedes the actual combat order. I don't think this is what -- what you said is in the doctrine of any military organisation anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, what about taking a break right now? We've been sitting for some time now. I think we can take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resume. Please be seated. Yes, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. If we can move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 660, 660A for the English version. The map on which the witness made a number of indications will be Prosecution Exhibit 661.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, take a look at Exhibit 660, which is a document from the Jure Francetic Brigade signed by Zivko Totic that is based on an order of the main staff and your order of the same date, referenced in the preamble, 01-1-184/93. Now, this particular order, General, essentially follows your order. I ask you, in this order from Zivko Totic, if you could take a look at number 4, and in number 4 of this order, Totic orders that his troops: "4. Stop any organised movement of Muslim forces with all available means. I hereby prohibit movement along these axes by armed individuals and groups in combat gear. They should be intercepted and disarmed if they fail to follow the order." Now, again, General, in raising your troops to combat readiness of the highest level, this was an extremely significant event militarily for the troops in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Please, could I just have a look at this order 660?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This order, document 660, is basically document 456/6, and it invokes the order 0166/93. Totic is giving the following orders, that he is prohibiting the movement of forces, and he says individuals and groups in that. However, I personally talked on the 19th of January to Dzemo Merdan, and I know that about ten vehicles passed by then, eight buses and two trucks, and they were moving from the direction of Zenica towards Gornji Vakuf, that is to say, that they were passing --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I must interrupt. My question was this -- General, my question was this: Raising combat readiness of your troops to the highest level was an extremely significant event, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was your last question. I listened carefully, and I wrote it down, but your first question was to comment on point 4 of the order of Mr. Totic, and I tried to answer that part. Raising combat readiness on any occasion is definitely a significant event, but no one tried to disarm anyone, nor did I order that at the meeting I had with my commanders, that is to say, to disarm members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I talked about the corps a few minutes ago, and I wish to note that at the time, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had 261.500 soldiers. In the 3rd Corps, it had 30.000 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, General, I ask you to stay with the particular question if you can. Now, at this particular --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sorry. But, Your Honours, may I complete my answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, General, complete your answer.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you. I would also like to say that this order was impossible to carry out because of this ratio of forces, and perhaps this order could have been carried out in the Operative Zone of northwestern Herzegovina or southeastern Herzegovina where the ratio of forces was different. But in my Operative Zone, it was impossible to carry out this order. It could not have been implemented in practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let us look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. So then the only thing that remains is how can we understand your question and how can orders be delivered when we know they cannot be executed. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let us look at what's transpiring in Gornji Vakuf on the same date as you give this order, and I give you another document which is part of the diary of Colonel Stewart on the 16th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 662.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I would like to refer to the second full paragraph on the entry for Saturday, 16 January, 1992, the paragraph that begins, Mr. Usher, with "The checkpoint ..." That's it. Stewart is referring to a trip through Gornji Vakuf and notes: "The checkpoint at the end of the mountain pass road was deserted. We proceeded carefully but fast from there into B Company's Base. There Alan briefed me on the situation. In his view the fighting could easily get much worse and it was continuing. The HVO had threatened to 'flatten' Gornji Vakuf unless the Muslims recognised it was part of Herceg-Bosna. I believe the HVO are at the bottom of this trouble." Now, in conjunction with this entry on the 16th, I'd like to turn our attention to the BritBat military information summary for the 16th.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 663.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I'll be referring to page 3, the bottom half of the document. It is the bottom half of the document for the entry on Gornji Vakuf for the date 16 January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It reads as follows: "Colonel Andreivitch the HVO Ops Zone commander read the following message from his commander, a general in Mostar: 'At the Geneva conference it was agreed that all provinces would be administrated by the leading ethnic group, in this area the Croats. The HVO and Croats fully intend to abide by this agreement. The HVO formally request that all BiH units return to their normal locations and that all BiH units from Jajce are removed from the area. In return, the Croats and HVO guarantee nothing will happen to the Muslim population less those suspected of, or accused of, war crimes. The Muslim population will be given full equality, but the BiH must be subordinate to the HVO. All troops must leave and fill in their trenches and all barricades are to be dismantled. Agic (Brigade Commander), Topcic (Area Commander), and Prije (Police Commander) are to be removed from command, their replacements may be picked by '3' Corps BiH, Zenica. All checkpoints are to be mixed as are police patrols. Gornji Vakuf is to be demilitarised and no one is to carry weapons in the town. The Bosnian media is to report the following in its bulletins (A list of commands that it should be reported that the HVO shelled no one, shot no one and did not burn any houses and that all these actions were carried out by the Muslims). With the immediate effect, the land border with Croatia is closed. There are two HVO brigades in Prozor supported by tanks and artillery ready to advance on Gornji Vakuf. You have until tomorrow to agree to all demands and put them into action or face the consequences. You are to send your reply via UNPROFOR. "Comment. The BiH have stated that they cannot agree to all the demands, the HVO do not appear to be willing to negotiate their demands. Therefore an escalation of the conflict seems inevitable. Comment ends." Now, General, this particular comment, this particular statement by Colonel Andrejevic in Gornji Vakuf to the Bosnian army authorities takes place on the 16th, the same day that you raised the combat readiness level for all of your brigades and independent units in Central Bosnia, and the question for you, General, is: Is that event, you raising the combat readiness and this ultimatim by the HVO in Gornji Vakuf, are those two events happening on the same day a coincidence or were you in communication with the authorities in Gornji Vakuf and were aware of what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My order, my command, it can be seen quite clearly here in document 456 that it was based on the order issued by the chief of the main staff. I got an order and that's the kind of order I issued. However, according to my order, not a single commander of a brigade that was under my command disarmed the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina because in my area it was impossible. The events in Gornji Vakuf are events in which the forces of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were taking place and the HVO forces of Northwestern Herzegovina. The relationship between the HVO forces and the forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Northwestern Herzegovina and Southern Herzegovina, the HVO was in a better position as compared to the BH army, and the 305th Mountain Brigade in Jajce that was fighting in Gornji Vakuf was a brigade that arrived from Zenica and Travnik to Gornji Vakuf, and that is an indicator that we did not carry out a blockade of organised movements of the forces of the BH army of the 3rd Corps that took part of the fighting in Gornji Vakuf. This 305th Brigade arrived from Zenica and Travnik, and in the report that you read to me, it was fighting in Gornji Vakuf, and on the 14th of February we agreed in a meeting that they should go back to Zenica. We agreed on this through the mediation of the U.N. and the European Monitors. I still have not understood from what you were saying about checkpoints. Whose checkpoint disappeared, of the BH army or of the HVO? I mean, from the introductory part that preceded your reading, because the entrance to Gornji Vakuf was in Bistrica. There was a BH army checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about your communications with Gornji Vakuf and look at a series of sit reps, situation reports, that were sent to you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 664, 664A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, 664 is a situation report from the Ante Starcevic Brigade in Gornji Vakuf sent to you, among others, noting, among other things as we read it: "This morning the enemy attempted to carry out an infantry attack from the direction of Voljice towards Galecnica and beyond towards Podgrade which our units successfully repelled. At the same time, the enemy, Balija," using the term Balija, "launched an artillery attack on Trnovaca, and Podgrade, and Pajic Polje area and the Ponir Zvizida area." The term "Balija" is, of course, a pejorative term for Muslims, isn't it, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is a derogatory term for Muslims. I listened carefully to the witness testimonies here and I know that they used it, but I know that nobody allege that I did use it, in other words, neither officially or unofficially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This was not what was said, General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This situation report is one of many situation reports you received from Gornji Vakuf during the conflict in Gornji Vakuf; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I endeavoured to be informed.
