I don't know what you mean by "many," but the report I have here, that is, the document 664, was sent on 18 January, 1993 and received at 2300, and that document in which I ordered the higher combat readiness was issued at 1145 pursuant to the order of the chief of the main staff which I had received. I don't know what you mean by "many." "Many" can be 500. "Many" can be 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you getting these reports on a daily basis from Gornji Vakuf, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I tried to get as much information to be as well-informed as possible. I wanted to receive them, if not daily, then as often as possible because I wanted to know. So --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. I must interrupt you because my time is limited. We will go to another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, I would ask you, if possible, to be more concise and to make shorter answers, if possible.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am trying, Mr. President, but for two years I've been isolated and without communication with other people and there is a lot of information and we're going through these documents very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I understand you perfectly, General Blaskic, but sometimes there is an overflow of explanation, an overflow of details which tend to make us lose the point, in a sense, and which tend to make us forget what was the question that was put to you. Each time you feel you need to make a comment to explain something, the Judges allow you to do so, but it shouldn't be something that you resort to every time, and it should not be to the detriment of what the Prosecution is doing. The Judges have to maintain a perfect equality of arms between the two parties while protecting your rights as an accused and also by making sure that you, as a witness, are granted your rights and respect your duties.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 665, 665A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this is another situation report coming from the Ante Starcevic Brigade. Again, a copy of it goes to you, and it is a day after the situation report that we just reviewed in Exhibit 664. So it would be accurate, finally, to say that the information that you were receiving from Gornji Vakuf was coming to your attention on a pretty regular basis, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You can glean from this information that this was a daily information which I received at 2230. I had been receiving such information on the events which had already transpired. This was not an obligation but just a gesture of goodwill, if you will, to inform me. He was informing everyone, including Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, let us look again at Exhibit 456, and this is Prosecutor's 456/6. This is your full combat readiness order of 16 January, 1993. Now, General, this particular order, as we reviewed previously, put independent units, the Bruno Busic formation, the Ludvig Pavlovic formation, and the Vitezovi formation on full combat readiness. My question to you, sir, is had you received a subordination order from the Ministry of Defence and from the chief of staff to put them on full combat readiness?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I referred to the order of the main staff's order 01-66/93 of 15 January, '93. I believe that this order regulated command of these units, that is, Vitezovi, Ludvig Pavlovic, and Bruno Busic. I do not know if a separate order had been received, but I know that this was the order of the main staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The subordination order that you received, what was it for?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The order on full combat readiness which I received from the main staff included all units in my zone, including these units. When some -- if you're asking me what is the purpose of this order, that means that if units had been attached to me, that I had the right to use these units and that I had a right to -- that I was authorised to task them, and that there are no other authorities in terms of disciplining them and punishing them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me show you Exhibit 250, and I would like to show you a reference point on 250. This is Defence Exhibit 250. Now, General, before we actually address Exhibit 250, when the Vitezovi and the Ludvig Pavlovic Brigade went to Busovaca in the latter part of January 1993, did members of those formations commit crimes in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Did they commit any crimes in Busovaca, is that the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't you refer to Exhibit 250 and look at 250. On the notation after the year "1993," you go down 3, it says: "Following the order number 2-014/93 of 26 January, 1993, a battle team of 15 soldiers, under the command of Major Berislav Sapina and Major Dragan Vinac was sent to the area of Busovaca."

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment. This is what page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just look for the heading that says "1993," General, and the third notation -- third paragraph after the year "1993."

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I found this third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, in the English it is page 4. Thank you. Now, this notation reflects that 15 Vitezovi soldiers were sent to the Busovaca area on the 26th of January, and my question for you, General, is: When those soldiers were in Busovaca, did those soldiers commit any crimes?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of this because on 26 January I was cut off in Kiseljak, in fact, as of 25 January, and I was not in the area of Busovaca and I do not have direct knowledge of whether they committed crimes or not. But this special purpose unit you can see refers in the first paragraph to the chief of main staff, which points to the chain of command which was a parallel one. Perhaps I may be allowed to quote the first paragraph. I did not issue an order for this combat group to go to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, did you later learn that the Vitezovi soldiers that were in Busovaca had committed crimes such as looting and the burning of Bosnian Muslim civilians' houses? Did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They did not report directly to me on their activities. This report, again, was not sent directly to my attention, but in a meeting in Busovaca which was chaired by the European Monitors, I heard from Dzemo Merdan that Vitezovi were solving problems by ultimatums. He did not specify how and where they did so, but of 25 January, 1993, I was blocked in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, when they were in Busovaca giving ultimatums or committing any other crimes, they were attached to you at that point, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were not sent to Busovaca under any order of mine and this is not the way we even registered our orders. Mr. Dzemo Merdan did not specifically say that the Vitezovi were solving problems by ultimatums in the Busovaca area. He was just talking in general about the area. I would have to go back to my notes on the meeting and see what he meant, but he referred to the area of Vitez. Now, these two are two neighbouring municipalities. They share the boundary, so they are close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, my question is this: You have put the Vitezovi on full combat readiness in Prosecutor's Exhibit 456/6, and when they went to the Busovaca area in late January, 1993, they were attached to you, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You see, there are two combat actions here: One is placing the Vitezovi on full combat readiness, that is, on 16 January, document 456/6, and this is what I did; then we have the other combat action, which is going to Busovaca to carry out a combat task. This is something else. On page 3 of the document which I'm holding here, the commander says that he -- under combat order 02-014/93 of 26 January, '93, a combat group was sent to Busovaca on a combat mission. I did not issue that order, but I did issue an order on carrying out a completely different thing. In this document, the commander of the Vitezovi also refers to the order of the chief of the main staff. This is the first paragraph in the document that you have given me. I can read this first document where you can see that the Vitezovi commander received two orders to raise combat readiness: One by the chief of the main staff and another one by me. We can read this at page number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, my question is very simple. You explained to us in great detail the concept of attachment, and my question for you is this: Was the Vitezovi attached to you, and, if so, when were they attached to you and for what purposes?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In order for this -- the Vitezovi were not attached to me for any combat activities in the Busovaca area, nor did I ask such a thing. As far as the combat readiness is concerned, the Vitezovi were part of -- had received the order, but then I see that they had received another such order which came from another source. It's one thing to issue an order to be on full combat readiness and it is another thing completely to issue an order about a combat operation, and I did not issue such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question for you, and I go back and will repeat my question, my question is, and I will read it: "Was the Vitezovi attached to you, and, if so, when were they attached to you and for what purposes?" We are referring to January of 1993, so I can be perfectly clear about this.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In January '93, as I already stated, pursuant to the order which I had received from the chief of the main staff, if the order referred to all units or if it was particularly specified including special purpose units, I then issued such orders, including to the special purpose units. However, the Vitezovi in January had their own chain of command which went directly from the defence department and the main staff --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. I do apologise. I hate to interrupt, and I will repeat the question again in case there's some lack of understanding on the question, and the question is as follows, and this is the third time: "Was the Vitezovi attached to you, and, if so, when were they attached to and for what purposes? We are referring to January of 1993, so I can be perfectly clear about this."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, my learned colleague has asked the question for the third time, and the witness had answered it twice in full. I think that he has stated perfectly clearly for what purpose they were attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're quite right here, Mr. Nobilo, but one has to admit that the witness is quite amazing because he manages to find his way around. You know, this is wartime. Here is a unit which is attached to him, he orders this unit to be in a state of combat preparedness or readiness, and when he has to go into combat, then suddenly the units are not under his orders any more. Maybe you are able to find your way around, but I am not. Maybe, Mr. Kehoe, perhaps if you put the question again you can help us understand better what was going on. In January '93, on the basis of an order emanating from the HVO, a different order from what was derived from the Vance-Owen Plan, from that order, I see that you have the competence to order maximum combat readiness orders for all formations, including the Vitezovi, and yet when these formations go into combat action, you are suddenly not the one who they are submitted to, under the orders whom they find themselves. Maybe the Prosecutor can help us see clearly through this by putting to you another question or maybe there is another document which could help us. Maybe there is a document showing how difficult it was to exercise this commandment. Maybe, indeed, it was very difficult to exercise this kind of commandment. This would also allow us to take into account the objection of Mr. Nobilo, because it is true that the question was put to the witness three times and that it is a bit tiring.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Let us look at the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 666, 666A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this is a very short order from Milivoj Petkovic dated 19 January, 1993 going to the Vitezovi Special Purposes Unit and to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command. "Order: The Vitezovi Special Purpose Unit, PPN, shall be assigned on all matters to Colonel Tiho Blaskic. I forbid any independent action. This order shall remain in force until I personally change it." Signed, "Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, here we are. It wasn't necessary to put the same question thrice. Now we are in a situation where we can try to understand. Mr. Kehoe, what is your question now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is, General, that when you told the Judges that the Vitezovi, when they conducted combat operations in Busovaca in January 1993, weren't attached to you, that, in fact, wasn't true, because they were attached to you; isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Attachment is something that is done for each combat activity or operation or action, and I am looking at this document here. I think that it was done in order to prevent them from doing anything independently. Then it says that it shall remain in force until the chief of staff personally changes it, but I must say that I was not responsible for their actions in Busovaca on 26 January, '93, and I was not even in Busovaca on 26 January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This order, General, subordinates the Vitezovi to you in all matters. Do you see that on the first line?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I see, but this order makes no mention of the time frame. It is dated 19 January, but it does not specify until when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General, I don't think there's any need to spend more time on this issue. I think we should go on to another document. I think that this order -- well, it seems that you consider that it does not imply what? Maybe I should take this the other way around. Let me remind you that this order that is submitted to us relates to you directly. Your name appears in this order. As Judge Rodrigues has just pointed out to me, the last sentence is quite clear, "This order will remain in force until" General Petkovic decides it should not be maintained any longer. We are not military experts. Maybe I should put the question the other way around. How could it be possible that the Vitezovi not be subordinated to you? What is it that makes it possible for General Petkovic not to place the Vitezovi under your commandment?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, there were two possible solutions: One is that this resubordination, attachment, referred to a certain combat operation or any activity, and that then after that, the subordination, the attachment was no longer there, and the Vitezovi became independent again; the other possibility is that the order arrived from General Petkovic saying that the attachment of the Vitezovi thus ends. So there are at least two solutions that are possible. If the attachment took place due to certain activities, then as soon as this activity is completed, then automatically this unit goes back to its regular situation. If I were to look at this document, document 250, in greater detail, I believe that we could see here that there are some very short periods when the unit is attached and then when it is no longer attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a minute, General.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We are not here in a military academy. We are not here drawing conclusions from hypotheses. We were not present at the time. You tell us there could be some solutions. I'm unable to follow you on that ground. This is not speculation. We are not trying to see what meaning can be attributed to this. You are the one who is directly concerned by this. If this is your answer, and it may be your choice to make this your answer, then I put it to the Prosecutor that maybe we should go on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Shahabuddeen has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Just before we move on to another document, General, let me put this to you: The Vitezovi were engaged in Busovaca, in action there on the 26th of January; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From this document, I can see that that is so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: If, on the 27th of January, General Petkovic had asked you for your report accounting for the actions of the Vitezovi, would you have said to him, "Sorry. They are not under my command"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If General Petkovic had sent an order to me for a specific action that the Vitezovi were attached to me for that action, I would have sent him an operative report on that action, including the unit of the Vitezovi. However, if the unit was not attached to me, I would have informed him only on that which I knew on the basis of the operative report. I would also report to him that the unit had acted independently, according to their own assignments or according to the assignments given by a superior. Because I have in this report, something I've just found now, that they were going to Stolac on the orders of Bruno Stojic, Minister of Defence, in October of 1992. This is down south in southern Herzegovina. At that time, I didn't even know that that unit was going there. I needed soldiers for Jajce. That unit went on the orders that they had received to carry out assignments at the front line of southern Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, should I understand you to be saying this, that in addition to General Petkovic's order of the 19th of January, he had to issue another document to you in the form of an attachment order relating to the specific operation at Busovaca before you could regard yourself as having authority over the Vitezovi in relation to that action? Is that the position, that you needed another document?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, when the resubordination of a unit is requested, that is usually for carrying out a particular activity, that is to say, particular combat action, and resubordination attachment is regulated in terms of its beginning and its end. The beginning is when the order is received, when the commander of the unit that is being attached reports that he received this assignment, and the end is after the assignment is carried out or after the operation is over, if a wider operation is planned. The unit goes back to its original position. It is quite similar in all armies, allied armies and others. It is regulated similarly. When a unit is attached, it does not lose all its independence. The one who takes it over only has the right to use it in combat and issue an assignment to it, without the other authority in terms of giving orders. That is what we did in terms of attachment. For example, had I planned a combat operation for the 26th of January, I would have addressed Brigadier Petkovic saying that, "I would like the Vitezovi to be attached to me for carrying out that particular assignment," but I did not plan a combat operation on the 26th of January, and for the attack, I did not request the attachment of the unit of the Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I'm trying very hard to follow you, General. Should I understand you to mean that on the 26th of January, the Vitezovi were free to act independently of you in relation to any activities they carried out at Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that I personally, since I spent time in Kiseljak, did not issue an order to the Vitezovi to act on the territory of Busovaca. But having said so, I'm not claiming that the Vitezovi had not received an order from a different instance, because in this report, in this report, 250, they are referring to many orders from the chief of the main staff, from the defence department, the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I tell you what's riveting my attention at this time, I see the first line on this order of 19 January, 1993, that the Vitezovi were being reassigned in all matters to you, in all matters, and in the second line, I read that General Petkovic is forbidding any independent action, presumably any independent action by the Vitezovi, with the further implication that they were now only to act dependently on you. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say that at that time, at least 300 good military policemen were needed in order to carry out this forbidding of independent action. This was envisaged in this order, but the situation on the ground was quite different. But I'm saying again that at this point in time, I cannot recall what the reason was for the attachment concerned. Is it this independent action? Because most of the incidents happened in Vitez and Novi Travnik where the PPN units figured prominently. We had some reports where the assistant for security mentioned that these units were the protagonists of incidents and that they were persecuting real Croats in that territory and that they figured prominently in these conflicts and problems. So in terms of disturbing public law and order in this area and in terms of the worsening of the general security situation, this attachment was carried out, but I also believe that it was very difficult to carry out this order. However, this, at any rate, is not an order. I never sought an order for the 26th of January to have the Vitezovi attached to me so that I would carry out attack action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No questions from Judge Rodrigues. Therefore, Mr. Kehoe, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, on this same day that you received this subordination order from General Petkovic, I ask you to take a look at Exhibit 250 and look at the notation for the 19th of January, 1993, and it reads as follows: "On 19 January 1993, the PPN 'Vitezovi' and the unit 'Ludvig Pavlovic' are engaged in reconnaissance and the gathering of intelligence about the movement of Muslim forces." Now, is that your order that those units are following, General? If it's not your order, who ordered these units to engage in reconnaissance and gather intelligence about the movement of Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not recall who issued this, but document 250 was not addressed to me. It was addressed to the main staff of the HVO. But in this order from the 16th of January, 1993, combat readiness was raised, and reference is made in point 8 that the entry of all persons should be prohibited, et cetera, and possibly reconnaissance and observation may have been reinforced. I cannot recall whether I personally issued such an order or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I ask you to take a look back at Prosecutor's Exhibit 658, if we could. This is Bruno Stojic's order of 15 January, 1993. In point 3 of that order of Bruno Stojic, it notes that: "Unit members of the HVO armed forces and BH army referred to in point 2 of this order who refuse to leave the region and acknowledge the superior command shall be regarded as members of a paramilitary unit and shall be disarmed and arrested." On number 7, the deadline for that is 1900 on the 20th of January, 1993. Now, with a deadline of 1900 on the 20th of January, 1993, with a threat to disarm and arrest Bosnian Muslim soldiers who would not subordinate themselves to the HVO, you are getting ready, through the orders on reconnaissance, you are getting ready for combat, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already stated that the BH army also received such an order and that the order certainly did produce high tensions. I also said that I did not order disarming of BH army members, nor did the disarming -- nor was it carried out according to my orders, because I never issued such orders. The relations between the BH army and the HVO in Central Bosnia was very much in favour of the BH army. I could not have disarmed 200.000 soldiers. Can I please see this order, document 658, please, of 15 January?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I please see the order of the chief of the main staff of 15 January?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is document 659.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if the witness can have document 659.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 659 is the order from General Petkovic, is it not, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President. 658 being the order from Minister Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Point 7 of the document 659, mention is also made that contact should be established with the BH army commanders in order to establish joint commands. The deadline here mentioned was extended by several days, as far as I know. So it was not 21, but it was extended. However, regardless of all that, I did not issue any orders to my commanders to start disarming BH army members, because we were David to their Goliath in Central Bosnia. It would have been an unreasonable thing to have done, whereas that was not the case in the northwestern and southeastern Herzegovina Operative Zones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Rodrigues has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, did you inform General Petkovic of what you have just told us, namely of the difficulties you were facing, of the impossibility you found yourself in to execute this order in your Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as the general relations of forces --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Did you inform General Petkovic of the difficulties you found yourself in? Did you inform him of the fact that it was impossible for you to execute this order for the precise reasons you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed him that I would call a meeting, and I was waiting for an agreement on implementation of the order. I could not have implemented it without it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you may continue. Thank you, Judge Rodrigues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let's just take this sequence. On the 16th of January you put all these units on combat readiness. On the 19th of January, the Vitezovi is subordinated to you for all purposes. On the 19th of January, the Vitezovi go out and do reconnaissance. On the 20th is the deadline for the BiH to disarm in your area. Now, quite clearly, General, as of the 19th you were getting ready for combat operations to commence on the 20th, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There's nothing said about the combat operations. The only thing mentioned was that both the HVO and the BH army be attached. What happened to this order is that it raised the tensions. It was like pouring gas on a fire, but there were no combat preparations for combat operations involved in this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, to follow up on Judge Rodrigues's questions, did you tell your commander, Milivoj Petkovic, that you're not going to disarm the BiH soldiers in your area and that you were not going to arrest them when they refused to disarm? Did you tell him that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I just said that I called a meeting because of this order, and that I informed the General that I would call the meeting, and that I was waiting for an agreement between the two chiefs of staff. In other words, I was waiting for the Generals Petkovic and Halilovic to reach an agreement on how to implement this order at all. For me, from the point of view of the forces that we had, it was not implementable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, do you have any documentation to support the fact that you informed General Petkovic that you could not comply with his order of 15 January? Do you have any documentation to support that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not have the document here, but in my operational report for that day I believe that I did send it. I have also hoped that General Petkovic will testify here and he would be able to tell more about this. But I know that a separate record was kept on this and the meeting that I had with my commanders, all my commanders. I even have a specific date and time when this meeting was held and when we discussed how to freeze this order because of the situation we had on the ground, because the order as we had it was absolutely not implementable at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us look, General, at another reference of events from the 19th of January and, again, this is the diary of Lieutenant-Colonel Stewart.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The meeting with my brigade commanders regarding this order was on 16 January at 1200.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 667.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this is again an English document, and I will read it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm interested in the first paragraph, Mr. Usher, under "Tuesday, 19 January." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Tuesday, 19 January. Things are getting very tricky indeed at the moment. The HVO are apparently threatening to go 'all out' in Gornji Vakuf and even expand the conflict to up here. Enver Hadzihasanovic, commander 3 Corps, BiH army, has appealed to me to recover Merdan from Gornji Vakuf and this I agreed to do. He was pulled out with a Warrior escort this morning amid reports that the HVO had mined the road overnight. False. People are now saying there is a deadline for violence to commence in the Vitez area too, that deadline being midnight tonight." The fact was that the deadline was on the 20th, wasn't it, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've been listening to these reports on the situation in Gornji Vakuf and I can only say that except for the daily summaries, I have no further information on this but that the situation and the positioning of the HVO in Gornji Vakuf was totally different vis-a-vis the position of the BH army in relation to the BH army in Central Bosnia. The HVO was completely inferior in Central Bosnia in general. If you're talking about the incidents and acts of violence on both sides, the BH army refused to allow us to rotate our troops to the front line against the Serbs. In other words, they denied us the passage. This is when the barricades were cropping up everywhere. I thought that we would have most problems in Vitez and Novi Travnik. However, we were able to stabilise the situation in both of these places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Shall I continue, Mr. President, or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you have any other questions you would like to put to the witness on that particular issue or document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Not that particular document. I was going to move to yet another document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In that case then we will suspend the hearing, and we will resume our work tomorrow morning at 10.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
